claims.claim: Won the 2026 Ballon d'Or on Monday 26 October at the London Palladium, first Englishman to win in about 25 years
claims.note: UEFA gives the date and venue (London Palladium Theatre); Sky says first English winner in 25 years.

claims.claim: Bayern's fourth Ballon d'Or winner after Beckenbauer, Müller and Rummenigge
claims.note: Source lists the same three names.

claims.claim: Born 28 July 1993, so 33 years old
claims.note: Wikidata date of birth 28 July 1993; Khel Now calls him 33-year-old.

claims.claim: Travelled from London to Munich for Tuesday training, as Aaron Danks said

claims.claim: Bayern teased a special welcome; Allianz Arena to shine in gold

claims.claim: Bundesliga clash with Borussia Dortmund on Saturday 31 October

claims.claim: FA profile: 36 league goals in 31 appearances, 100 goals in 104 competitive games for Bayern, European Golden Shoe, third straight top scorer award

claims.claim: Sky Sports called him the bookmakers' favourite before the ceremony, quoting no odds

claims.claim: Potential fee of €120m (£104m), described as potential, not confirmed; would have surpassed €80m (£68m) paid for Lucas Hernández from Atlético in 2019

claims.claim: Tottenham's 2019 article: 25 England goals in 40 caps

claims.claim: Tottenham's 2022 feature cited Jimmy Greaves' 266 goals for Spurs

claims.claim: England debut against Lithuania in March 2015; scored 79 seconds after coming off the bench

valueNote: Adds a dated timeline of the Bayern extension status, the NST quotes, and the FA and Bundesliga figures with primary-source links. The English version is the original, so it is not judged against a translation.
summary: All checked claims are supported by the opened sources. No wrong, unsupported, outdated or unreachable claims. Bayern extension is correctly described as agreed in principle; a web search found no official announcement as of 28 October 2026.
